newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM B767 engine changes boost cargo uplift.
newsitem.headline: KLM B767 engine changes boost cargo uplift.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV is modifying its Boeing 767 aircraft to enable them to carry more cargo, an airline spokesman told Reuters.
By making relatively minor modifications to the engines of the B767-300 ERs the aircraft can carry more than nine tonnes of extra cargo, he added.
The increase in the B767s engine capacity enables the aircraft to improve the take-off weight from 172.2 tonnes to 181.4 tonnes.
He said the decision was taken because of strong demand for freight capacity on the U.S. market.
These aircraft are deployed on routes that need the extra uplift such as routes to Atlanta and Memphis, he added.
Eight of the company's B767s have already gone through the process and two which are on order will also be modified.
